First, we find the roots of the characteristic polynomial:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+144 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-144 \\ \lambda  & =\pm 12\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =P\operatorname{cos}⁡12x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡12x\end{aligned}
$$

We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(\frac{\pi }{8})=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-Q=1\,⟹\,Q=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{8})=24,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-12P\operatorname{sin}⁡12x+12Q\operatorname{cos}⁡12x.
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{8})=24$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}12P=24\,⟹\,P=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡12x-\operatorname{sin}⁡12x.
$$
